sanskrit: atha nāvaṃ suvistīrṇāṃ naiṣādīṃ rāghavānujaḥ āruroha samāyuktāṃ pūrvam āropya maithilīm
english: Then Rāghava's younger brother, having first helped Maithilī board, himself boarded the well-appointed, spacious Niṣāda boat.

sanskrit: sumantraṃ caiva sarathaṃ sthīyatām iti lakṣmaṇaḥ uvāca śokasaṃtaptaḥ prayāhīti ca nāvikam
english: Lakṣmaṇa, burning with grief, said to Sumantra together with his chariot, "Stay here," and said to the boatman, "Row on."

sanskrit: tatas tīram upāgamya bhāgīrathyāḥ sa lakṣmaṇaḥ uvāca maithilīṃ vākyaṃ prāñjalir bāṣpagadgadaḥ
english: Then, having reached the bank of the Bhāgīrathī, Lakṣmaṇa spoke these words to Maithilī, his palms joined in reverence, his voice choked with tears.

sanskrit: hṛdgataṃ me mahac chalyaṃ yad asmy āryeṇa dhīmatā asmin nimitte vaidehi lokasya vacanīkṛtaḥ
english: "There is a great thorn lodged in my heart, O Vaidehī, that I have been made an instrument of public reproach by the noble and wise one on this account."

sanskrit: śreyo hi maraṇaṃ me 'dya mṛtyor vā yat paraṃ bhavet na cāsminn īdṛśe kārye niyojyo lokanindite
english: "Death today, or whatever lies beyond death, would be better for me. I should not have been employed in such a task as this, which is condemned by all the world."

sanskrit: prasīda na ca me roṣaṃ kartum arhasi suvrate ity añjalikṛto bhūmau nipapāta sa lakṣmaṇaḥ
english: "Be gracious to me; you ought not to be angry with me, O lady of excellent vows." Saying so, with joined palms, Lakṣmaṇa fell to the ground.

sanskrit: rudantaṃ prāñjaliṃ dṛṣṭvā kāṅkṣantaṃ mṛtyum ātmanaḥ maithilī bhṛśasaṃvignā lakṣmaṇaṃ vākyam abravīt
english: Seeing him weeping, his palms joined, desiring his own death, Maithilī was seized with great distress and spoke these words to Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: kim idaṃ nāvagacchāmi brūhi tattvena lakṣmaṇa paśyāmi tvāṃ ca na svastham api kṣemaṃ mahīpateḥ
english: "I do not understand this at all — tell me the truth, Lakṣmaṇa. I see that you yourself are not at ease. Is the king well?"

sanskrit: śāpito 'si narendreṇa yat tvaṃ saṃtāpam ātmanaḥ tad brūyāḥ saṃnidhau mahyam aham ājñāpayāmi te
english: "Were you cursed by the king, that you are afflicting yourself with such grief? Tell me in my presence. I command you."

sanskrit: vaidehyā codyamānas tu lakṣmaṇo dīnacetanaḥ avāṅmukho bāṣpagalo vākyam etad uvāca ha
english: Thus urged by Vaidehī, Lakṣmaṇa, his heart broken, face cast downward, his throat thick with tears, spoke these words.

sanskrit: śrutvā pariṣado madhye apavādaṃ sudāruṇam pure janapade caiva tvatkṛte janakātmaje
english: "Having heard a most terrible reproach spoken in the midst of the assembly, and likewise throughout the city and the countryside, on account of you, O daughter of Janaka —"

sanskrit: na tāni vacanīyāni mayā devi tavāgrataḥ yāni rājñā hṛdi nyastāny amarṣaḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtaḥ
english: "— those words which the king laid to heart, casting indignation behind him, are not to be spoken by me before you, my lady."

sanskrit: sā tvaṃ tyaktā nṛpatinā nirdoṣā mama saṃnidhau paurāpavādabhītena grāhyaṃ devi na te 'nyathā
english: "You, who are blameless, have been abandoned by the king through fear of the citizens' censure — it cannot be otherwise, my lady — and I am the one entrusted with this."

sanskrit: āśramānteṣu ca mayā tyaktavyā tvaṃ bhaviṣyasi rājñaḥ śāsanam ājñāya tavaivaṃ kila daurhṛdam
english: "I am to leave you at the edge of the hermitages, having received the king's command — such, indeed, is the cruel wrong done to you."

sanskrit: tad etaj jāhnavītīre brahmarṣīṇāṃ tapovanam puṇyaṃ ca ramaṇīyaṃ ca mā viṣādaṃ kṛthāḥ śubhe
english: "But this is the sacred and beautiful forest of austerity of the brahmarṣis on the bank of the Jāhnavī — do not give way to despair, O auspicious one."

sanskrit: rājño daśarathasyaiṣa pitur me munipuṃgavaḥ sakhā paramako vipro vālmīkiḥ sumahāyaśāḥ
english: "This foremost of sages, the supremely renowned brāhmaṇa Vālmīki, is the dear friend of King Daśaratha, my father."

sanskrit: pādacchāyām upāgamya sukham asya mahātmanaḥ upavāsaparaikāgrā vasa tvaṃ janakātmaje
english: "Come to the shelter of this great soul's feet and dwell there happily, O daughter of Janaka, intent on fasting and spiritual practice."

sanskrit: pativratātvam āsthāya rāmaṃ kṛtvā sadā hṛdi śreyas te paramaṃ devi tathā kṛtvā bhaviṣyati
english: "By abiding in the vow of devotion to your husband, and keeping Rāma ever in your heart, your highest good, O lady, will come about by doing thus."

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā dāruṇaṃ janakātmajā paraṃ viṣādam āgamya vaidehī nipapāta ha
english: Having heard Lakṣmaṇa's terrible words, the daughter of Janaka, Vaidehī, fell to the ground overcome by the deepest anguish.

sanskrit: sā muhūrtam ivāsaṃjñā bāṣpavyākulitekṣaṇā lakṣmaṇaṃ dīnayā vācā uvāca janakātmajā
english: She lay as if unconscious for a moment, her eyes clouded with tears; then the daughter of Janaka spoke to Lakṣmaṇa in a faint voice.

sanskrit: māmikeyaṃ tanur nūnaṃ sṛṣṭā duḥkhāya lakṣmaṇa dhātrā yasyās tathā me 'dya duḥkhamūrtiḥ pradṛśyate
english: "This body of mine was surely created for sorrow by the Creator, Lakṣmaṇa, since the very form of suffering is so manifest in me today."

sanskrit: kiṃ nu pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ pūrvaṃ ko vā dārair viyojitaḥ yāhaṃ śuddhasamācārā tyaktā nṛpatinā satī
english: "What sin was committed in a former life, or what husband was I separated from, that I, a chaste woman of pure conduct, have been abandoned by a king?"

sanskrit: purāham āśrame vāsaṃ rāmapādānuvartinī anurudhyāpi saumitre duḥkhe viparivartinī
english: "Before, O Saumitre, I lived in the hermitage following at the feet of Rāma, and yet even while attending upon him I was plunged in sorrow."

sanskrit: sā kathaṃ hy āśrame saumya vatsyāmi vijanīkṛtā ākhyāsyāmi ca kasyāhaṃ duḥkhaṃ duḥkhaparāyaṇā
english: "How, O gentle one, shall I dwell in a hermitage forsaken and alone? And to whom shall I tell my grief, I who am wholly immersed in sorrow?"

sanskrit: kiṃ ca vakṣyāmi muniṣu kiṃ mayāpakṛtaṃ nṛpe kasmin vā kāraṇe tyaktā rāghaveṇa mahātmanā
english: "What shall I say among the sages? What wrong have I done the king? For what reason have I been abandoned by the great-souled Rāghava?"

sanskrit: na khalv adyaiva saumitre jīvitaṃ jāhnavījale tyajeyaṃ rājavaṃśas tu bhartur me parihāsyate
english: "Indeed I would relinquish my life today in the waters of the Jāhnavī, O Saumitre, but the royal lineage of my husband would become an object of ridicule."

sanskrit: yathājñāṃ kuru saumitre tyaja māṃ duḥkhabhāginīm nideśe sthīyatāṃ rājñaḥ śṛṇu cedaṃ vaco mama
english: "Do as commanded, O Saumitre; leave me, who am the companion of sorrow. Let the king's command be obeyed — but hear this word of mine."

sanskrit: śvaśrūṇām aviśeṣeṇa prāñjaliḥ pragraheṇa ca śirasā vandya caraṇau kuśalaṃ brūhi pārthivam
english: "Bow your head and, with joined palms upraised, reverently salute the feet of all my mothers-in-law without distinction, and convey my good wishes to the king."

sanskrit: yathā bhrātṛṣu vartethās tathā paureṣu nityadā paramo hy eṣa dharmaḥ syād eṣā kīrtir anuttamā
english: "As you conduct yourself toward your brothers, so conduct yourself always toward the citizens — this is the highest dharma, and this would be matchless glory."

sanskrit: yat tvaṃ paurajanaṃ rājan dharmeṇa samavāpnuyāḥ ahaṃ tu nānuśocāmi svaśarīraṃ nararṣabha yathāpavādaṃ paurāṇāṃ tathaiva raghunandana
english: "Whatever you may win from the citizens through righteousness — O bull among men, O joy of the Raghus — I do not grieve for my own body as I do for the censure of your citizens."

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvantyāṃ sītāyāṃ lakṣmaṇo dīnacetanaḥ śirasā dharaṇīṃ gatvā vyāhartuṃ na śaśāka ha
english: While Sītā was speaking thus, Lakṣmaṇa, his heart broken, bowed his head to the earth and was unable to utter a single word.

sanskrit: pradakṣiṇaṃ ca kṛtvā sa rudann eva mahāsvanam āruroha punar nāvaṃ nāvikaṃ cābhyacodayat
english: Having made a reverential circumambulation of her, he boarded the boat again, weeping loudly, and urged the boatman on.

sanskrit: sa gatvā cottaraṃ kūlaṃ śokabhārasamanvitaḥ saṃmūḍha iva duḥkhena ratham adhyāruhad drutam
english: Having crossed to the northern bank, weighed down with the burden of grief, dazed as it were by sorrow, he swiftly mounted the chariot.

sanskrit: muhur muhur apāvṛtya dṛṣṭvā sītām anāthavat veṣṭantīṃ paratīrasthāṃ lakṣmaṇaḥ prayayāv atha
english: Turning back again and again to look at Sītā standing helpless on the far bank, wringing her hands, Lakṣmaṇa then departed.

sanskrit: dūrasthaṃ ratham ālokya lakṣmaṇaṃ ca muhur muhuḥ nirīkṣamāṇām udvignāṃ sītāṃ śokaḥ samāviśat
english: As Sītā, distressed, gazed again and again at the chariot growing distant and at Lakṣmaṇa, grief entered into her deeply.

sanskrit: sā duḥkhabhārāvanatā tapasvinī yaśodharā nātham apaśyatī satī ruroda sā barhiṇanādite vane mahāsvanaṃ duḥkhaparāyaṇā satī
english: That ascetic woman, bearer of glory, bowed down by the burden of sorrow, seeing no lord at her side, wept with a great cry of anguish in that forest resounding with the cries of peacocks, she the chaste one wholly consumed by grief.

sanskrit: sītāṃ tu rudatīṃ dṛṣṭvā ye tatra munidārakāḥ prādravan yatra bhagavān āste vālmīkir agryadhīḥ
english: Seeing Sītā weeping there, the young disciples of the sages ran to where the blessed Vālmīki, foremost in wisdom, was seated.

sanskrit: abhivādya muneḥ pādau muniputrā maharṣaye sarve nivedayām āsus tasyās tu ruditasvanam
english: The sons of sages, having saluted the sage's feet, all reported to the great seer the sound of her weeping.

sanskrit: adṛṣṭapūrvā bhagavan kasyāpy eṣā mahātmanaḥ patnī śrīr iva saṃmohād virauti vikṛtasvarā
english: "Blessed one, a woman never seen here before, the wife of some great soul, is crying out in distress like Śrī bewildered, her voice broken."

sanskrit: bhagavan sādhu paśyemāṃ devatām iva khāc cyutām na hy enāṃ mānuṣīṃ vidmaḥ satkriyāsyāḥ prayujyatām
english: "Blessed one, kindly look upon her — she is like a goddess fallen from the sky; we do not know her to be a mortal woman. Let proper honor be rendered to her."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā buddhyā niścitya dharmavit tapasā labdhacakṣuṣmān prādravad yatra maithilī
english: Hearing their words, the knower of dharma, his inner sight acquired through austerity, having ascertained the truth with his wisdom, hurried to where Maithilī was.

sanskrit: taṃ tu deśam abhipretya kiṃ cit padbhyāṃ mahāmuniḥ arghyam ādāya ruciraṃ jāhvanītīram āśritaḥ dadarśa rāghavasyeṣṭāṃ patnīṃ sītām anāthavat
english: The great sage, having gone a little way on foot toward that place and taken his welcoming offering, reached the lovely bank of the Jāhnavī, and there he saw Sītā, the beloved wife of Rāghava, standing helpless.

sanskrit: tāṃ sītāṃ śokabhārārtāṃ vālmīkir munipuṃgavaḥ uvāca madhurāṃ vāṇīṃ hlādayann iva tejasā
english: Vālmīki, foremost of sages, spoke gentle words to Sītā, afflicted by the weight of grief, as if refreshing her with his radiance.

sanskrit: snuṣā daśarathasya tvaṃ rāmasya mahiṣī satī janakasya sutā rājñaḥ svāgataṃ te pativrate
english: "You are the daughter-in-law of Daśaratha, the faithful queen-consort of Rāma, the daughter of King Janaka — welcome to you, O lady devoted to your husband."

sanskrit: āyānty evāsi vijñātā mayā dharmasamādhinā kāraṇaṃ caiva sarvaṃ me hṛdayenopalakṣitam
english: "Even as you were coming, you were known to me through my absorption in dharma; and the entire cause of this has been perceived in my heart."

sanskrit: apāpāṃ vedmi sīte tvāṃ tapolabdhena cakṣuṣā viśuddhabhāvā vaidehi sāmprataṃ mayi vartase
english: "I know you to be sinless, Sītā, through the sight gained by austerity. You are of pure heart, O Vaidehī — now you are under my care."

sanskrit: āśramasyāvidūre me tāpasyas tapasi sthitāḥ tās tvāṃ vatse yathā vatsaṃ pālayiṣyanti nityaśaḥ
english: "The female ascetics established in penance not far from my hermitage will care for you always, dear child, as a calf is cared for."

sanskrit: idam arghyaṃ pratīccha tvaṃ visrabdhā vigatajvarā yathā svagṛham abhyetya viṣādaṃ caiva mā kṛthāḥ
english: "Accept this welcoming gift; be at ease, freed from anxiety. Come as if arriving at your own home, and do not give way to grief."

sanskrit: śrutvā tu bhāṣitaṃ sītā muneḥ paramam adbhutam śirasā vandya caraṇau tathety āha kṛtāñjaliḥ
english: Having heard the sage's words, most wonderful indeed, Sītā saluted his feet with bowed head and said "So be it," with joined palms.

sanskrit: taṃ prayāntaṃ muniṃ sītā prāñjaliḥ pṛṣṭhato 'nvagāt anvayād yatra tāpasyo dharmanityāḥ samāhitāḥ
english: Sītā, with joined palms, followed behind the departing sage; she followed to where the female ascetics, ever constant in dharma, dwelt in composure.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā munim āyāntaṃ vaidehyānugataṃ tadā upājagmur mudā yuktā vacanaṃ cedam abruvan
english: Seeing the sage arriving with Vaidehī following him, they came forward filled with joy and spoke these words.

sanskrit: svāgataṃ te muniśreṣṭha cirasyāgamanaṃ prabho abhivādayāmaḥ sarvās tvām ucyatāṃ kiṃ ca kurmahe
english: "Welcome to you, O foremost of sages; long has it been since you came, O master. We all salute you — speak, what shall we do?"

sanskrit: tāsāṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā vālmīkir idam abravīt sīteyaṃ samanuprāptā patnī rāmasya dhīmataḥ
english: Hearing their words, Vālmīki said to them: "This Sītā has come — she is the wife of the wise Rāma."

sanskrit: snuṣā daśarathasyaiṣā janakasya sutā satī apāpā patinā tyaktā paripālyā mayā sadā
english: "She is the daughter-in-law of Daśaratha, the virtuous daughter of Janaka, sinless, abandoned by her husband — she is to be protected by me always."

sanskrit: imāṃ bhavatyaḥ paśyantu snehena parameṇa ha gauravān mama vākyasya pūjyā vo 'stu viśeṣataḥ
english: "You all look upon her with the deepest affection. Out of respect for my word, let her be honored by you especially."

sanskrit: muhur muhuś ca vaidehīṃ parisāntvya mahāyaśāḥ svam āśramaṃ śiṣyavṛtaḥ punar āyān mahātapāḥ
english: Having consoled Vaidehī again and again, the greatly renowned sage of great austerity returned to his own hermitage, accompanied by his disciples.
